## Purpose

The Alembic revision chain for the backend's SQLAlchemy schema â€” a single linear history from an
empty database to the current head (`0040`).

Every deployment and every local `alembic upgrade head` depends on it; no other module writes
DDL.

## Shape

One file per revision, hand-numbered `0001`-`0040` (`0003` is absent â€” never cut) with an
explicit `down_revision` chain, so the chain stays single-head and `alembic upgrade head` is
deterministic.

- [0001_initial_schema.py](../../backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial_schema.py) â€” baseline: `users`, `chat_sessions`, `messages`, `workflow_runs`,
  `revoked_tokens`.
- `0002`-`0009` â€” small additive columns/tables (handoff credentials, token usage, user
  tier/admin/preferred-model, workflow model id) plus a `0009` no-op that documents a
  schema-debt audit and re-anchors the chain.
- `0010`-`0015` â€” the Phase 3/5 Artifact_Store era: `workflow_artifacts` (thin store) lands in
  `0010`, workflow tables (`workflow_clarifications`, `workflow_memory`, `workflows`) in `0011`,
  `workflow_runs` grows its execution-gate/session columns in `0012`, `pipeline_run_id` collapses
  into `id` in `0013`. `0014` adds the durable typed-artifact schema (`artifact_refs`,
  `workspaces`, `run_events`, `run_capabilities`) and backfills a default workspace per existing
  run. `0015` is the **one deliberately destructive migration**: it drops the now-orphaned thin
  `workflow_artifacts` table once every reader moved onto `artifact_refs`.
- `0016`-`0020` â€” capability-hardening / multi-agent era: `validation_results`, `gate_events`,
  `hook_runs` (`0016`); `repositories` + `mcp_credentials` (`0017`, Phase 9 repo workflows);
  `exec_runs` audit table (`0018`, Phase 10 sandbox exec); `subagent_runs` (`0019`, Phase 11
  fan-out); `wave_runs` (`0020`, Phase 12 wave scheduler).
- `0021`-`0027` â€” product-feature columns: saved user workflows reusing the dormant `workflows`
  table (`0021`), deliverable mimetype/filename (`0022`), launch-time `selections_json` (`0023`),
  `run_events` uniqueness backstops (`0024`), `deep_link_nonces` (`0025`), per-child task identity
  on `subagent_runs` for crash resume (`0026`), OpenDesign `od_context_json` for resumed
  od_ppt/prototype runs (`0027`).
- `0028`-`0037` â€” repair, index, and workflow-runtime tail: `0028` repairs 0024/0025 drift;
  `0029` reconciles duplicate `run_events` before enforcing uniqueness; `0030` adds the
  `(user_id, created_at)` history index; later revisions continue the runtime schema.
- `0038`-`0040` â€” Cognito-only user cutover: `0038` fails closed unless every user is cleanly
  Cognito-linked, makes `cognito_sub` non-null, drops `password_hash`/`auth_provider`, adds
  `users.status`, and creates the pending-deletion retry queue; `0039` adds selected user-FK
  cascades; `0040` gives legacy non-revoked API keys the existing expiry policy.
  **Current head: `0040`.**

## Why this shape

The normal discipline is additive migration, with explicit, reviewed cutovers as the exception.
`0015` drops the retired thin artifact store; `0038` intentionally drops local credential columns
only after a fail-closed Cognito-link preflight. Future migrations must call out any comparable
non-additive step, its recovery boundary, and its downgrade limitation.

Runtime-owned tables carry `owner_id` + `workspace_id` so `ScopedStore` can default-deny them.
`pending_cognito_deletions` is a documented operational exception: it is created after the user
row is deleted and therefore records a deleted-user snapshot rather than a live owner/workspace
pair. Status/kind/provider columns remain free `String`, never `sa.Enum`, unless a migration
states otherwise.

`0028`/`0029` exist because a stamped-but-unapplied revision is a real failure mode in this
history â€” they are worked examples of detecting and repairing that drift without a destructive
re-stamp.

Not attempted here: no down-migration squashing, no consolidated baseline â€” **the full chain is
kept** so `alembic downgrade` stays meaningful at any point in history.
